The '''Scottish football champions''' are the winners of the highest league in [[Football in Scotland|Scottish football]], namely the [[Scottish Football League]] (SFL) from 1890 until 1998, the [[Scottish Premier League]] (SPL) from 1998 until 2013 and the [[Scottish Premiership]] thereafter.

The SFL was established in 1890, initially as an amateur league until professionalism in Scottish football was  legalised in 1893.<ref name="Davies158">{{cite book |last=Davies |first=Hunter |title=Boots, Balls and Haircuts: An Illustrated History of Football from Then to Now |isbn=1-84403-261-2 |year=2003 |publisher=Cassell Illustrated |page=39}}</ref> At the end of the [[1890–91 in Scottish football|first season]], [[Dumbarton F.C.|Dumbarton]] and [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] finished level on points at the top of the table. The rules in force at the time required that the teams contest a play-off match for the championship, which finished in a 2–2 draw, and the first ever championship was thus shared between two clubs, the only occasion on which this has happened.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/scotchamp.html |title=Scotland – List of Champions|access-date=5 March 2008 |date=22 August 2007|archive-date=22 September 2008 |website=[[RSSSF]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080922133240/http://www.rsssf.com/tabless/scotchamp.html|url-status=live}}</ref> In 1893, a lower division was formed, with the existing division renamed Division One. The higher tier continued during [[World War I]] but the league was suspended altogether during [[World War II]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/scotall.html |title=Scotland – List of Divisional Movements|access-date=5 March 2008 |date=3 January 2007|archive-date=27 April 2009 |website=[[RSSSF]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090427003921/http://www.rsssf.com/tabless/scotall.html|url-status=live}}</ref>  

Although there were several short spells when a third level was created, the two-division structure remained largely in place until 1975, when a major re-organisation of the league led to a new three-tier setup and the creation of a new [[Scottish Football League Premier Division|Premier Division]] at the highest level. In 1998, the teams then in the Premier Division broke away to form the SPL, which supplanted the Premier Division as the highest level of football in Scotland.<ref>{{cite web |work=www.scotprem.premiumtv.co.uk |url=http://www.scotprem.premiumtv.co.uk/page/History/0,,10002,00.html |title=History |publisher=Scottish Premier League |access-date=17 December 2013 |archive-date=2 February 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070202041829/http://www.scotprem.premiumtv.co.uk/page/History/0%2C%2C10002%2C00.html |url-status=dead}}</ref> The SPL and SFL merged in 2013 to form the [[Scottish Professional Football League]] (SPFL), which branded its top division as the Scottish Premiership.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23435136 |title=SPFL: New Scottish league brands unveiled |date=24 July 2013|access-date=24 July 2013 |publisher=BBC |work=BBC Sport|archive-date=28 July 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130728010657/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/23435136|url-status=live}}</ref>

Throughout its existence the championship of Scottish football has been dominated by two [[Glasgow]] clubs, [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] and [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]]. The two rivals, who are collectively known as the "[[Old Firm]]", have claimed the vast majority of league titles and there have only been five seasons in which neither finished in the top two, most recently in the [[1964–65 in Scottish football|1964–65 season]].  As of 2026, Celtic have won 56 titles and Rangers 55, while no other club has won on more than four occasions. No club outside the Old Firm has won the title since the [[1984–85 in Scottish football|1984–85 season]], when [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] won the Premier Division under the management of [[Alex Ferguson]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/aberdeen-stars-dougie-bell--1852483 |title=Aberdeen stars Dougie Bell & Neil Simpson: We wouldn't have believed our SPL victory would be last for non-Old Firm team |first=Colin |last=Duncan |work=Daily Record |publisher=Trinity Mirror |date=25 April 2013 |access-date=17 December 2013 |archive-date=16 October 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131016063547/http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/aberdeen-stars-dougie-bell--1852483 |url-status=live}}</ref> The current 41-year period of dominance by the Old Firm is a record; the previous longest streak was 27 years, between 1904 and 1931. Each of the Old Firm clubs has managed a run of [[Nine in a row|nine consecutive championships]]: Celtic from 1966 to 1974 and again from 2012 to 2020,<ref name=ends20 /> and Rangers from 1989 to 1997. 

Both of the Old Firm clubs have also claimed the [[Double (association football)|double]], by winning the league and the [[Scottish Cup]] in the same season, on many occasions.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.celticfc.net/pages/history |title=Brief history |website=www.celticfc.net |publisher=Celtic FC |access-date=17 December 2013 |quote=1988: Celtic celebrate the centenary season (1987/88) by winning the first "double" in 11 years. The accomplishment marks the 35th league title, and the 28th Scottish Cup. |archive-date=10 May 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160510143304/http://www.celticfc.net/pages/history |url-status=live}}</ref> As of the end of the [[2025–26 in Scottish football|2025–26]] season, Celtic have won 22 doubles and Rangers 18.  The only other club to have won a league and Scottish Cup double is Aberdeen, in [[1983–84 in Scottish football|1983–84]].<ref name = double>{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/miscellaneous/doublerec.html |title=Doing the Double!|access-date=20 April 2013 |date=18 April 2013|archive-date=26 November 2015 |website=[[RSSSF]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151126184235/http://www.rsssf.com/miscellaneous/doublerec.html|url-status=live}}</ref>  Both Old Firm clubs have completed a [[Treble (association football)|treble]] (Celtic 8 times; Rangers 7) by also winning the [[Scottish League Cup]].<ref name = double /><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.rangers.premiumtv.co.uk/page/HistoryDetail/0,,5~456,00.html |title=1946–1970 An Historic Treble |publisher=Rangers FC |work=www.rangers.premiumtv.co.uk |access-date=17 December 2013 |archive-date=1 July 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070701165826/http://www.rangers.premiumtv.co.uk/page/HistoryDetail/0%2C%2C5~456%2C00.html |quote=In 1948–49, Rangers became the first team to win the League, the Scottish Cup, and the League Cup in one season. It was the first glorious treble in Scottish football. |url-status=dead}}</ref>  In the [[1966–67 in Scottish football|1966–67 season]], Celtic took all three domestic trophies, and also won the [[UEFA Champions League|European Cup]] to complete the only [[The Quadruple|quadruple]] to date.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2007/feb/28/theknowledge.sport |title=The sulkiest football walk-offs ever |work=The Guardian |date=28 February 2007|first1=James|last1=Dart|first2=Nicky|last2=Bandini|first3=Sean|last3=Armstrong|access-date=5 March 2008|archive-date=9 January 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080109053642/http://football.guardian.co.uk/theknowledge/story/0,,2022367,00.html|url-status=live}}</ref>
